samples.summary: Real backend error messages are now discarded on every non-envelope failure (401/403/404/400 validation), because the backend has no global exception filter and returns Nest's default `{message, error:'Not Found', statusCode}` bodies
samples.evidence: The backend's v1 API throws plain Nest exceptions and no global exception filter exists (grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters` in packages/backend/src returned nothing). So the *common* failure bodies the CLI receives are framework-shaped, not the envelope: packages/backend/src/api/v1/files.controller.ts:141 `throw new NotFoundException('Document has no file')`, files.controller.ts:81 / documents.controller.ts:109 `throw new ForbiddenException('This API key does not have write access')`, workspace-scope.guard.ts:28 ForbiddenException, cells.controller.ts:58 `NotFoundException('Tab not found')`. Before this change `wafflebase files download <id>` / `files upload` / `docs import` printed that body, so the human/agent-readable cause ("Document has no file", "This API key does not have write access") reached stderr. After it, `upstreamErrorJson` (formatter.ts:127-132) and `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:109) drop the body entirely and emit only `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'|'ERROR', message:'HTTP 404'}}`. Only the code shape is fixed; the diagnostic text is lost for every real backend error except the two hand-built envelopes (TYPE_MISMATCH, SESSION_EXPIRED). docs/design/cli.md:1039 documents the opposite intent for backend failures — "(original message preserved)". The fix belongs on the new helpers: carry the framework body's `message` (and `statusCode`) into the envelope's `message` instead of throwing it away.

samples.summary: Adding index.html's own families (Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono) to the font gate makes every visual capture, in every section, hard-depend on fonts.googleapis.com resolving within 10s
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/index.html:12 requests Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono on every page load, so those FontFaces are registered for *all* harness pages, not just slides sections. Previously the polled set was only the four families useGoogleFontsLink() injects (so `document.fonts.check` matched nothing and returned true trivially on the ~200 non-slides captures). Now, if the css2 stylesheet loads but the font binaries fail or are slow (restricted-network CI, cold cache), the faces stay unloaded/errored and the new `waitForFunction(..., {timeout: 10000})` at verify-visual-browser.mjs:384 fails for every one of the 220 baselines under packages/frontend/tests/visual/baselines/, not just the two sections that drifted. The swallowed `.catch(() => {})` on `fonts.load` (line 374) removes the previous fast failure, so the symptom becomes a timeout per page. Worth confirming the visual lane has egress to fonts.googleapis.com; otherwise the enumerated set should be limited to families the section under capture actually registers, or the poll should tolerate errored faces.

samples.summary: Moving the font settle to after section mount can change what the captured pixels contain, but no baseline PNGs are updated in this change
samples.evidence: waitForFontsReady now runs after the section-ready wait (verify-visual-browser.mjs:431-434) and additionally blocks on Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono at four weights. Any baseline that was captured while one of those faces was still on the fallback will now render with the webfont and mismatch. The 220 committed baselines in packages/frontend/tests/visual/baselines/ are outside this diff and none are shown as regenerated; if any drifted section's baseline encodes the fallback rendering, the visual lane will report a diff rather than a fix.

samples.summary: Sibling commands that receive the same TYPE_MISMATCH envelope still flatten it, so the centralized guard is only half-adopted (explicitly a non-goal, noted for traceability)
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md:1029 promises `sheets.cells.get` on a doc reports code TYPE_MISMATCH, but packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:25 still does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`, discarding the backend envelope the new `forwardUpstreamError` was written to preserve; packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:41 flattens it to a bare message. docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:56 lists these as an intentional non-goal, so this is a consistency note, not a regression from the diff.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. `upstreamErrorJson` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:123-133) and `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:100-110) discard any non-envelope response body, emitting only `HTTP <status>`. The backend genuinely produces framework-shaped bodies for the common failures: grep for `ExceptionFilter|useGlobalFilters` in packages/backend/src returns nothing and packages/backend/src/main.ts:30-79 registers no global filter, while controllers throw plain Nest exceptions carrying the diagnostic text (packages/backend/src/api/v1/files.controller.ts:141 'Document has no file', :81 'This API key does not have write access'; document/document-file.controller.ts:46,52,92). Those bodies do reach the helper: http-client.ts:261-267 parses the JSON error body into `res.data`, and files/download.ts:56-58, files/upload.ts:217, docs/import.ts:165,195,212, notes/import.ts:159,186,208, slides/import.ts:195,238,255 pass it directly to `upstreamErrorJson`; commands/docs.ts:197,249, commands/notes.ts:148,195, commands/slides.ts:154,197 route through `forwardUpstreamError`. The prior contract is corroborated in-repo: test/upstream-error.test.ts:218-221 records that these paths previously printed `res.data` verbatim, and docs/design/cli.md:1039 documents '(original message preserved)'. This is a behaviour change to exported helpers affecting consumers outside the diff, i.e. in-lane for blast radius; only the two hand-built envelopes (api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:42-88) survive. No guard or alternate path restores the message, so no refutation ground applies.
